2608.06417.title: Latent Fact-Checking: Detecting Misinformation through Activation Engineering
2608.06417.paper_summary: The proliferation of misinformation online has driven demand for scalable detection systems. While most existing approaches rely on surface-level linguistic features or external knowledge retrieval, we examine truthfulness as a geometric property of a language model's representation space. We introduce a misinformation detection framework grounded in activation engineering, which leverages the latent geometry of transformer models. Our approach elicits a misinformation direction in the residual stream by contrasting activations from paired truthful and false statements, following the difference-in-means principle of Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA). At inference time, the last-token activation of an unseen claim is projected onto this direction, and the projected representation is fed to an Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) for classification. The procedure requires no fine-tuning of the backbone model, no external evidence retrieval, and no task-specific supervision beyond the contrastive pairs used to estimate the direction. We evaluate the method across 11 models from the Gemma, Llama, and Qwen families, ranging from 270M to 12B parameters, on three fact-checking benchmarks: AVeriTeC, LIAR, and FACTors. The falsehood direction is recoverable across model scales and architectural families, and last-token projection matches or surpasses zero-shot and few-shot prompting baselines on LIAR and FACTors, with the largest gains observed for smaller models. Performance on AVeriTeC is more limited, which we attribute to its evidence-grounded labeling scheme. These findings provide evidence that truthfulness is a structured, linearly separable concept in the latent space of pretrained language models, and point toward interpretability-driven misinformation detection as a practical complement to retrieval-based pipelines. The code is available on https://github.com/Malta-Lab/LaFaCt.
2608.06417.paper_summary_zh: 網路上錯誤資訊的擴散推動了對可擴展檢測系統的需求。雖然大多數現有的方法依賴於表面層的語言特徵或外部知識檢索，但我們將真實性視為語言模型表示空間的一種幾何特性。我們介紹了一種基於激活工程的錯誤資訊檢測框架，該框架利用了Transformer模型的潛在幾何特性。我們的方法通過對比配對的真實和虛假陳述的激活，來引出殘差流中的錯誤資訊方向，遵循對比激活加法（CAA）的均值差異原則。在推理時，未見聲明的最後一個標記激活被投影到這個方向上，然後將投影表示輸入到多層感知器（MLP）進行分類。該程序不需要對主幹模型進行微調，不需要外部證據檢索，也不需要超出用於估計方向的對比對的任務特定監督。我們在三個事實核查基準上評估該方法，分別是AVeriTeC、LIAR和FACTors，涵蓋了來自Gemma、Llama和Qwen家族的11個模型，參數範圍從270M到12B。虛假方向在模型規模和架構家族中都是可恢復的，最後一個標記的投影在LIAR和FACTors上與零-shot和少-shot提示基準相匹配或超越，對於較小的模型觀察到最大的增益。對於AVeriTeC的表現則較為有限，我們將其歸因於其基於證據的標記方案。這些發現提供了證據，表明真實性是在預訓練語言模型的潛在空間中一個結構化的、線性可分的概念，並指向以可解釋性驅動的錯誤資訊檢測作為基於檢索的管道的實用補充。代碼可在 https://github.com/Malta-Lab/LaFaCt 獲得。
